## Details

### elekloader

Mod loader: user supplies the stock OS file, the tool builds the custom .syx locally. Device table in the README (3016dca, 2026-11-08): Digitakt mk1 and Digitone mk1/Keys supported; Digitakt II 1.17 and Digitone II 1.12 experimental; Octatrack 1.40C supported (linkable core boots on an MKII); Model:Cycles and Model:Samples 1.13 supported (builds work on both units); Analog Rytm MKII 1.74 supported; Analog Four MKII 1.56 experimental proof of concept (hook bus, mod storage, unused DDR and recovery checked on a unit). Canonical repo is unclear: the forum post also embeds github.com/elekloader/elekloader (web app at elekloader.github.io/elekloader); forks exist (AvroraPolnareff, naturarum, toonst, simonjohansson); none is listed, as none has changes of its own. Forum: builder issue reported 2026-10-19. Licence GPL-2.0-or-later. 2026-11-10 (8daa2ea): the shop's list, forms and bots moved to elekloader/shop (#338); mods are submitted there. machine-pages 1.8-1.10, machines-dn1 0.5/0.6 and machines-dn2 0.5 add mono machines and MIDI CCs (emulator-tested per TESTS.md). The linker now refuses odd jump targets into mod RAM after a Digitakt II froze at boot (I61). The README offers a Windows .exe; not every release carries the macOS .dmg. 2026-11-10 (main): core-ar2 0.13 opens the Rytm MKII's TEST slots 44-52 to mod machines, adds per-voice trig and velocity getters, screen calls through stock's routines and per-mod knob ids; machine-pages 1.7 tagged. 2026-11-12 (main): core-a4mk2 0.6 brings core-ar2 0.10-0.13's foundations to the Analog Four MKII (field defaults, the modified mark, the project-save event, payloads, knob looks, screen calls) and a 37.7 MB mods' area. Builds pick older core or helper versions by themselves when a mod patches a place a newer one took (Tone+FX's Digitakt files and Digi EQ 1.0c link with DT1 core 4.0 only; OB-1 0.6 with machine-pages 1.2), and released versions stay available while a listed mod needs them. 2026-11-13 (main): a third file family, ELE2, for the Analog Rytm MKI OS 1.74 (Modwerk's Rytm MKI research holds the measurements behind the profile); the README's table also names 1.73, the profile only 1.74. core-ot 0.9-0.40 opens about 40 more Octatrack events and tables to mods (mutes, sequencer moments, LFO waves, popup rows, PATTERN SETTINGS and PERSONALIZE rows, the playback increment, card file calls, the engine task's jobs, a block to DSP core 1). 2026-11-15 (FORMAT, SDK, CORES): std1 'standard events': a mod that sets events std1 subscribes to device- neutral event names, each core maps them to its own tables, and a subscription the core does not map is refused at link time; std1 and native mods link in one build. core-a4mk2 0.7 is the first core with it and adds native A4 events for knob turns, the analog voice frame and modulation edits. A frame-check build that copied one voice's analog frame words over another's silenced track 1 and was fixed in 0.3 (unit or emulator not stated). 2026-11-16 (docs/CORES.md, DRIVE.md, FORMAT.md, core-dn1 README): on the Digitone mk1 the build descriptor now carries the stock bytes of each flashed range (ABI 1.2), and TELOS's linker refuses a +Drive mod site that is not stock on the unit, overlaps the flashed build or another mod, or a region outside a free area (link codes 21-28). core-dn1 5.4's core_stock_info copies the OS image to 0x44200000 before the OS runs. 2026-11-17 (ADAPTING, FORMAT, core-ot, settings-ot, dspload-ot, core-a4mk2 READMEs): core-ot 0.41/0.42 add 16 Octatrack events (tempo, scenes, card mount and USB DISK MODE, previews, recorder commands, pages, track select, windows, crossfader, pattern select and edits, arrangement); new dspload-ot 0.2 sends DSP code at run time (mod.json `dsp_load`), also for TELOS card mods; refusal code 23 `early` for a site the OS ran before the +Drive or card link. On the Analog Four MKII the lock service is now checked on a unit. 2026-11-18 (v0.11.0, docs/DRIVE.md, CORES.md, drive-loader-a4mk2 and drive-loader-ar2 READMEs): v0.11.0 ships the newest core of every device, core-a4mk2 0.9 included. The Analog Four MKII gets its own +Drive mods loader (drive-loader-a4mk2 0.1, not yet run): stock 1.56 keeps the +Drive as raw sectors with no file system, so the loader keeps its own two-copy store in sectors stock never addresses. The Rytm loader (0.6) now reads each file into the +Drive area itself (a 64 KB floor replaces the 512 KB staging buffer), and +Drive mods may hold storage fields, sites over the OS, claims, tables of their own, knob ids and std1 subscriptions where the build's descriptor flags allow (descriptor ABI 1.3). drive-loader-ar2's README asks for core-ar2 0.14 while core-ar2's mod.json at the tag reads 0.13. New A4 MKII check mods for live recording, the sequencer and moments (read as expected in the emulator, 2026-11-14). 2026-11-20 (ADAPTING, CORES, DRIVE, FORMAT; core-ar2 README and SKIPS.md; core-dt2, core-dn2, core-a4mk2, drive-loader, smpl-machines READMEs; new AR2 and DT2 examples): core-dt2 1.1 keeps mods' project and kit data in bytes stock writes as zeros (191 bytes a kit), adds value rows, a per-frame parameter event and key LEDs; core-dt2 1.2 and core-dn2 0.5 add what TELOS needs on the unit (card ready, project save and load, crash, restart, task list), checked in digikit's emulator only, not yet on a unit. core-ar2 0.15: knob faces, mod folders in the +Drive sample browser, pad strikes before stock and LED colours, a held USB input gain step, note ends, track mutes, DIN MIDI out, machines given slots by count; 0.16: four optional CPU skips, off at boot (silent voices, idle sample layer, the UI's dynamic_cast, idle delay and reverb), two of which change the sound slightly, and GLOBAL submenus. The linker hands out machine slots, page ids and mod-declared id pools by count, kept in the lockfile. New smpl-machines (a SMPL page machine layer) and smpl-knob-c. Five new Rytm check examples and kit-memo-dt2. core-a4mk2 0.10's core_project_keep lets the A4 loader's APPLY & RESTART keep unsaved project changes. core-a4mk2's README now says core 0.2's pages drew identically on a unit (OS 1.56). 2026-11-22 (AGENTS, ADAPTING, CORES, DRIVE; core-ar2, drive-loader-ar2 and drive-loader-a4mk2 READMEs and PAGE.md; five new Rytm check examples): core-ar2 0.17 brings the std1 standard events to the Analog Rytm MKII and adds knob flags: a mod's own knob can open a destination list as LFO DEST does (only the list bit is honoured). core-ar2 0.18 adds restart calls. drive-loader-ar2 now needs core-ar2 0.18, marks mods with saved data with * and has APPLY & RESTART, as the A4 loader. The new Rytm check examples (std, std-midi, ui, voice, knob-flags) are built and linked only. The core-ar2 README restates its OS-upgrade restart check: analog-emu hung on 5 of 15 upgrades without core's restart routine and 0 of 15 with it (0 of 30 with the panel link paced as on a unit). 2026-11-24 (docs/DRIVE.md, drive-loader READMEs): drive-loader-ar2 0.12 and drive-loader-a4mk2 0.2 give mods a versioned +Drive payload API (drive_payload_abi, count, at, find, info with id, length and sha256, dl_payload_read; imported weakly by sidecar-core) and lock a loaded mod's file until the next boot: an upload over it is kept as <name>.new and swapped in at the next boot with the new CRC written first, so a power cut cannot leave the new file under the old CRC; the MODS page shows UPDATE or LOST and refuses DELETE (IN USE: RESTART FIRST). On the A4 reads that span a card sector go straight into the caller's buffer (a 4 KB read takes 7-10 card reads, not 64-80). 2026-11-25: core-ar2 0.20 adds `ev_store_adopt` (a sound or kit saved with another layout or before core storage is handed to its mod once as it loads; example adopt-check-ar2) and mod storage fields can be pinned to fixed bits with `offset`. core-ar2 0.21 moves the Rytm MKII mods area to 0x47B48000-0x47FFF000 (4.7 MB), above stock 1.74 USB audio feedback ring at 0x47B47440-0x47B47480, which stock rewrites while a host has the audio alternate setting selected; 0.11-0.20 started at 0x47B10000 and reached that ring once a build passed 221 KB. 2026-11-26 (docs/ADAPTING.md, DRIVE.md, core-ar2 README and SKIPS.md, examples/drive-machine-check-ar2): core-ar2 0.22 lets +Drive mods add machines too: `core_machines` now spans all 19 hidden slots 34-52 (was 10, slots 34-43), and the Drive Loader's entries reach the machine table after `ev_boot_drive`, after which the project loads again (with 0.21 they never reached it). New example drive-machine-check-ar2 tests this without a +Drive. 2026-11-27 (docs/ADAPTING.md): the build profiles pin -std=gnu17, so a gcc that defaults to C23 (15 and later) builds the same code; a mod's own cflags may name another standard.

_Latest seen (2026-10-31, secondary directories): altstrument.org and the repo (read 2026-10-31): canonical repo is github.com/elekloader/elekloader (183 commits, 103 stars, GPL-2.0-or-later); web app moved to elekloader.github.io/elekloader; the Mac app was absent from v0.9.0 because signing secrets need renewing. v0.9.0 cores: core-4.1 and core-4.1-os1.54 (Digitakt mk1), core-dn1-4.1.1 and -os1.44 (Digitone mk1), core-ar2-0.8 (Analog Rytm MKII 1.74), core-ot-0.8 (Octatrack 1.40C), core-mc-0.3 (Model:Cycles), core-ms-0.1 (Model:Samples), core-a4 0.1-0.4 (Analog Four MKII 1.56). Kit 0.7.0 catalog: 19 cores, 88 mods. machine-pages 1.2/1.3/1.5 need core 3.0+ on Digitakt mk1 and refuse NEIGHBOR 0.6, SOPHIE 1.1.13 and digichain-based machine mods beside them; fxkit 0.1 gives Digitone effect mods a shared mixer, two LFOs, pattern p-locks and a CPU guard; core-dn1 4.1 adds ev_note_queue; kit 0.6.0 gives 4.0 cores larger RAM areas (256 KB Digitakt, 1.25 MB Digitone). docs/ includes AGENTS.md, DEVICES.md, MACHINES-DN2, SHARC-DN2, CORES, FORMAT, BUILDING, ADAPTING (not all read yet - see hardware/MINING.md). The earlier irpina/elekloader repo is where the author's older releases lived._

### Modwerk (formerly Octamod)

2026-11-12: the Octatrack card firmware builder is retired: modules reach an Octatrack only through the Modwerk base, over USB or as one set file (MODWERK0.SET) on the card; Tuner, Stem Rec and Temp Save paused until they have base versions; Spectrum, Modulation, Character and MIDI Scenes removed for good; CPU-rendered machines get a budget (CPU FULL) after FM Synth froze an MKII (I79); POLY8 and FM Synth carry a Heavy CPU badge; checks refuse writes into the stock DELAY table and odd jump targets; the DT2 base hides the raw +Drive block write from modules; Octatrack modules moved to sdk/octatrack/modules; new experimental Crossfader and Live Looper for the Digitakt I (OS 1.54) and Amiga, a tracker-style sample machine, for the Octatrack. 2026-11-11/12: the Octatrack base and USB installs are open to everyone (first install still from the card, at most 20 modules per set, 24 since 2026-11-14; Tuner, Stem Rec and Temp Save card-only); USB Audio is off unless the set has the USB Audio module; skipping modules at boot moved from FUNC to holding PROJ at power-on (MKI keeps FUNC); the octabam pin is frozen (Modwerk follows only elekloader upstream); Analog BD 0.1.7 has a new 909 model; base-update and SYNTIZ incidents I75 and I76. 2026-11-09/10: Octatrack beta: the silence after USB DISK MODE (finding 72) was the base mistaking stock's DSP pause for a stall, fixed (I69); FM Synth with many FLEX tracks no longer loses the audio on PLAY; the Octatrack page asks for a power cycle when the DSP has stopped; Temp Save 0.1.0 withdrawn from USB installs (card build stays). Modwerk also loads effects onto Zoom MultiStomp pedals now (ZDL files over USB; not an Elektron device). Browser-based hub, builds locally from the user's own stock OS. Browse mods by device, forum with a section per device, shared SDK. Dubspot (13 Oct): several modules are still early prototypes. last_activity = date of the Dubspot article, not a forum post. 2026-11-02: three Analog Rytm MKII modules by npp1993 moved into the library (Pipo Loop 0.1.1, Sample RATE 0.1.0, Silent Pad+Trig Settings 0.6.0, all experimental, OS 1.74; linkable together with core-ar2 0.7, Filter Hz and Loop Sync; the packages themselves not yet run on a unit). `_submissions/` takes no new modules. The Octatrack USB beta also works on the MKI. 2026-11-03: the site now lets you download a built Analog Rytm MKII .syx (after confirming you know how to get back to stock); new Rytm module quick-velocity-aftertouch-assign with a verification note. Zoom pedals: an effect whose group+ID clashes with one already on the pedal is moved to a free local Delay ID 958-1023 (ID only in the ZDL header at 0x40-0x41, no checksum); two effects with the same group and ID froze an MS-70CDR at boot until its ROM was reprogrammed. 2026-11-04/05: Rytm MKII downloads on (records); npp1993's Control In Actions (footswitch or 0-5 V gate on EXP/CV IN as ACTION for MUTE and more) and Quick Velocity+Aftertouch Assign join the library, Silent Pad+Trig Settings 0.7.0; euclidean 1.1.6 for Digitakt I 1.53/1.54 reported working on a unit by sumedho (all cases, save/reload, power cycle). 2026-11-08 to 11-10 (74c9eb2): Rytm library gains comp-preview, kit-ab, lfo-rnd and voice-dac (from rytm2_mods, unit runs on the Modwerk base), ctrl-in-perf and scene-mutes (from rytm-mods-src 0017/0018, unit runs T208/T210/T221), Improved Machine Browser and MIDI Mute; the Octatrack key bus moved to the tail of the first FX2 slot (checked on an MKI and an MKII); a Digitakt II audio scheduler is proposed (emulator only); Zoom MS-70CDR pedal work (out of scope here). 2026-11-12/13: Octatrack base: a stall record now keeps the 128 frames before it; an installed Sidechain no longer causes NO ROOM on every pick after a restart (I96); a new USB device revision (bcdDevice 0x0101) repairs Windows hosts that could not open the unit (I100); a machine engine's DSP price moved into its package; the base refuses a module machine or effect pick while the CPU meter is at 85 % or more; VECTOR 0.3.2 fixes a whole-bank reset (I95); SYNTIZ and Tape Echo get a Heavy CPU badge. Rytm MKII: the send-bus base gains digital voices; new Improved AMP and BD ANALOG (I97-I99). module:doctor covers Digitakt II modules; a Digitakt II pre-send render hook is proposed (emulator only). FRACT, an Octatrack granular machine draft by ex1010, has a functional unit report (2026-11-10). 2026-11-14 (second pass): the Digitakt II moved from research to preview: the site builds core 1.0 with library modules in the browser, downloads stay off, OS 1.17 only; the first DT2 library module is Track Names; DT2 phrase modules can continue phrases across empty steps, follow microtimed trigs and save settings in a project archive. Octatrack: a two-step base update for units whose RAM stage is too small; the CPU guard counts the picked machine's price and judges a stopped unit by its last playing load (I105); POLY8 0.3.3 and FM Synth 0.1.3 cost far less while installed on no track (FM Synth 0.1.3 also fixes track 1's LFO 3); `device:price` measures a module's cost; a new Octatrack Diagnostics page on the site. 2026-11-14 (changelog, verification): an Octatrack module set may hold 24 modules (was 20, still temporary); the base may grow to 1.5 MiB, so units on a base older than 2026-11-13 take it as two USB updates, and a base update retries up to four times when a reply goes missing before the write starts. New project and bank events (load, save, reload, new project, Part save and clear) let a module keep its own file beside the project. Amiga 0.3.0 (experimental) adds a SYNC stretch mode that follows the project tempo; in a RAM trial on an MKII an earlier build of it restarted after about 90 s on a twin that also carried a base change under test (I109). Filter Hz 1.2.1 (Rytm MKII, from rytm2_mods' port of 0008-filter-hz) widens the box behind a locked FRQ so kHz values fit; a maintainer ran it on a Rytm MKII on OS 1.74 on 2026-11-14. 2026-11-16 (changelog 2026-11-14/15, LINK.md, TEST_RUNNER.md): Rytm MKII development bases carry a SysEx USB link (screen, memory, keys, encoders, remote flash, and a boot from RAM with no flash write), and a test runner plays scripted cases on rytm-emu or a unit over it. Filter Hz 1.3.0 shows the FX track's delay and reverb HPF, LPF and reverb FRQ in Hz. 2026-11-17 (changelog 2026-11-16/17, verification, module docs): Octatrack base versions start at 0.7 (shown as MODWERK BASE 0.7 on the unit; 0.7.1 to 0.7.5 the same day): PROJ > MODWERK > MODULES switches installed modules on and off; a project remembers which machine each track uses, so a missing machine is named instead of playing FLEX; one module may use 288 KiB (was 128) and may borrow sample memory while installed; windowed modules such as Tuner can come over USB (base 0.7.5); packages are no longer refused for sharing byte runs with stock; every Octatrack module must name its CPU price (`resources.cpuPrice`); `module:doctor` reports DSP register writes against each hook site's contract; stall records name each DSP core's last packet. New Octatrack modules Kits and MIDI Scenes 0.3.0 (experimental ports of octabam's modules, short RAM trials on the owner's MKII); the Octakit draft is removed. New Digitakt I module CC Remap. Rytm MKII: a third base variant, voices; Ping Pong Loop folded into Improved SMPL 0.6.x; size-only updates of several modules run on the author's unit; Analog Rytm MKI builds are refused when the update exceeds the upgrade buffer or touches the boot-flash writers. Goal pages for contributors on the Digitakt II and the Syntakt (no Syntakt module yet). Field diagnostics 12-16 Nov: 87 units. A dialog on the site says the project's future is uncertain and asks for maintainers. 2026-11-18 (changelog 2026-11-07..17, verification, machine guides): Octatrack base 0.7.7 skips stock's delay work for tracks whose delay is silent (CPU meter 41 to 34 % with DELAY on every track); a machine's CPU price is now its mean cost per playing track (FM Synth 0.1.4: 6 %, seven tracks a Part); DSP voices book only what the bank's Parts use (core 0 up to 3,120 cycles); a shared scale file for Octatrack modules. Rytm MKII: sets linked by Modwerk's own linker may use 704 KiB or 3.7 MiB of DDR above the 128 KiB mod area; the voices base drops the FX lock words (1,752 B more for modules). Rytm MKI SDK guide published (research). Digitakt II: the site builds Modwerk's base 8650bb8a on core-dt2 1.1 (elekloader#221 at 0df8409), downloads still off; new modules MIDI Engine (Rytm), Euclidean Scale and Mute Latch (DT2), Vibrato (Octatrack, from octabam). Machine maintainers may now merge a machine's first module releases; pull requests that change a built package stay drafts until that build ran on a unit. The dialog saying the project's future is uncertain was removed. 2026-11-18, later (changelog, OCTATRACK_PACKAGE_DSP_HOOKS): Octatrack base 0.7.8 makes the per-track sound-source hook (DSP site 5) a chain (#1098): the base offers each track to every installed DSP track machine in turn and the first that owns it plays it, so a second DSP machine (BlackPyramids) can install over USB beside Analog BD; Analog BD's package and sound are unchanged. The key bus (option B) is merged (#737). 2026-11-19 (changelog 2026-11-14..19, DESKTOP_APP, MACHINE_RECIPE, HOOKS, MODULE_PERFORMANCE, arr-rows, butter- fingers, Digitone II verification): every contribution, core work included, now comes to Modwerk as a pull request, and every machine is to get a Modwerk base (Digitone II and Analog Four MKII included). Octatrack base 0.7.8 lets modules rest when unused; 0.7.9 adds a shared Part Edit menu and fixes an effect lost after a project load (I154). A desktop app (Electron, WebUSB and Web MIDI) is in development, Windows only so far, never run against a unit. Digitone II: core-dn2 0.3 builds booted on a second unit from Transfer, and stock 1.12 came back with a normal update; no Modwerk module can be built for it yet. Two stock Octatrack arrangement bugs found by Arr Rows (SB33, SB34). 2026-11-20 (changelog 2026-11-18/19, verification 2026-11-19 beta diagnostics, OCTATRACK_DRIVING, MODULE_PERFORMANCE, machines guide, micro-timing README/TESTING, Digitone II GOAL): most of the day's changelog is web app, agent board and tooling. Octatrack: base 0.7.9 is the site's base since 2026-11-18 (about nine units by 2026-11-19); base 0.7.10 is to add a refusal code of its own when a module's DSP claims meet a delay buffer (code 12) and to log which check refused a module at start. The card holds two set slots (MODWERK0.SET, MODWERK1.SET); a set loaded from the card is made the one the next boot prefers while the other stays for recovery. A live CPU/DSP load card on the site (USB). The machine guide now explains the frame guard's budget and how to count skipped renders. New draft Micro Timing 0.1.1-experimental (own_mods); its remembered row moved out of battery RAM into the module's own memory. Zoom MS-70CDR: Sync repairs an effect missing from the pedal's list; the list is written back only while the pedal stays connected. Digitone II: Modwerk's own linker knows OS 1.12 and links core-dn2 0.3 and 0.4 byte for byte as elekloader does, but refuses mods with DSP code; the site builds no Digitone II firmware yet. Base changes now collect in one draft pull request per machine, shipped by the owner after long tests on a unit; device reviewers (assigned per machine) approve first module releases. 2026-11-21 (changelog 2026-11-17..21, verification 2026-11-19..21, OCTATRACK_USB_AUDIO_MODULE, TEST_PROCEDURE, DIGITONE_II_OS_RESEARCH): Octatrack base 0.7.10 gives a DSP claim that meets a delay buffer its own refusal (code 12, naming the FX2 slot to move), logs which check refused a module at start, brings Analog BD back after a rolled-back trial (I178), lets Undo finish once a module's page is closed, and cuts the UI-tick cost of large sets; 0.7.11 (served) waits for a project load to finish before it changes the DSP's effects (I180) and rests unused machine and effect modules; 0.7.12 (staged) installs USB Audio 0.3.0 as one module configured on the unit instead of seven base variants (reconnect failures fixed on the way, I176, I177). Installed but unused modules may cost at most 0.2 points of the frame interrupt from now on, or must rest. Every module or base change now goes through one test procedure that the submitter runs; reviewers only read its record. A fast MIDI soak and a queue for the shared unit are new tools. New modules: kitbank for the Digitone (OS 1.44) and Screen Off for the Octatrack; Improved SMPL 0.6.3 and Direct Jump Kyoti 0.2.0 (V7.3). Digitone II: the research page names the MCF5441x, the SHARC+ boot over DSPI2 and the ARM core; the site can read a development base and upload a module to its RAM, but no Digitone II module exists yet. Also 28 Zoom MS-70CDR effects (not an Elektron device). 2026-11-22 (changelog 2026-11-21, verification 2026-11-21, MODULE_PERFORMANCE, MODULE_RESOURCE_GAUGES, TEST_PROCEDURE, OCTATRACK_DRIVING, effects guide, Grain, analog-bd and qperf docs, Rytm README): Octatrack base 0.7.13 judges a module machine pick on a busy unit by the CPU-meter points the machine adds (measured on a unit against Flex) instead of its frame price, which had refused Grain on a Part that played at 43.5 % on the owner's MKII. Module pages show measured CPU, DSP and memory figures where they exist and estimated tiers elsewhere. New track machine Grain (granular, up to six grains), measured at length on the owner's MKII; it still misses the frame deadline with 20-channel USB capture, and a panel freeze after one Grain trial is unexplained (I187). Under ot_emu the CPU meter reads 100 % from boot, so the emulator refuses every module pick. The effects guide explains the DSP56300 div half quotient. Rytm MKII: QPER Live Rec 0.3.0 follows pattern-length changes, BD ANALOG 0.2.2 drops the 808/909 badge, and Improved Performance (audio load 85.4 to 72.1 % on the author's unit) entered the library and was retired the same day, to be folded into the Rytm base. Every machine now runs one test procedure; Rytm unit steps run over its link with a RAM boot. Base work now goes to one cumulative draft per machine. 2026-11-23 (changelog 2026-11-22, verification 2026-11-22, MODULE_PERFORMANCE, MODULE_AUTHOR_UPDATES, Grain README/TESTING, Rytm README, Pad Pressure Fix README): testers run released Octatrack base 0.7.13; one logged a UI stop during playback with six modules installed (I191), and a Windows tester saw failed USB staging and a USB Audio trial rolled back at the reconnect (I192); the installer now retries claiming the returning interface. Grain 0.1.2 treats the sample as a ring and plays each grain 3 dB lower. Rytm MKII: package builds refuse audio code that needs over 512 B of stack; Pad Pressure Fix moves into the base. An unpublished Elemod update can be rolled back. 2026-11-24 (changelog 2026-11-19..24, verification notes): base 0.8 admits modules by frame time instead of the mean meter (renders capped at 122 % of a frame) and holds late frame entries so the DSP skips a frame instead of stopping (I198, I199); a USB re-attach watchdog; LCD capture over USB at 5-30 fps; USB audio input; Part Edit rows can hide; sample-editor SNAP; restore outcomes named on the Status page; the site engine can upgrade a Digitone II's OS over USB MIDI (no UI yet). Base stock fixes: three are Zac-Kyoti's MIT code from octatrack-kyoti-fw, the USB input receiver is copied from octabam. Open: FM Synth 0.1.5 keeps costing about 11 frame points after its notes (#2030), RAM boots not seen by the host about 1 in 3 (#1985), a card-save failure after a Keep on 0.8, a 0.7.12 stall and UI freeze on a tester's MKI. 2026-11-25 (changelog 2026-11-20..24): new base table `ot_settings` (PROJ > MODWERK > SETTINGS) for whole- instrument settings; Kits 0.1.1 needs base 0.8; Mute Modes 0.2.3, Scale Quantizer 0.1.5 and SYNTIZ 0.1.1 updated; a release dated from 2026-11-24 needs curve and admission evidence (only the owner can waive it); Python 3.12+ required; a widened identity gate caught 10 of 10 planted faults (old gate 1 of 10); device tools also drive an MKI (FUNC + MIDI opens the Part window). Base 0.8 stock fixes (SB10, SB12) passed on the owner's MKII; USB Audio INPUTS fail on Windows 10 (I205). Digitakt II: OS 1.17 saves a kit when only module kit data changed (2026-11-25, Euclidean Scale 0.2.0). 2026-11-26 (changelog 2026-11-23..25, verification 2026-11-23 and 2026-11-25, Model:Cycles SDK and LINK.md): Model:Cycles (OS 1.13) gets a Modwerk base in development, built from elekloader's core-mc 0.3 plus a key-LED hook; it carries a USB MIDI SysEx link (identity, audio load, diagnostics log, the Octatrack's runtime loader for RAM trials; development bases add memory reads, keys, encoders and a RAM boot) and ran flashed on a submitter's unit; no module yet, the page is beta-only and downloads are off, so the Model:Cycles is not in this entry's devices yet. Octatrack: new FX modules Mackity (Airwindows port) and Midiverb I/II (Alesis programs); an oversized module set is now stopped before sending (787 kB of module memory on the unit); `device -- boot` refuses to RAM-boot over an unconfirmed two-slot update (each restart spends one of its two starts, I219); a test procedure with a preflight, an emulator rehearsal and a Part put-back; a shared DSP gate harness and an Airwindows port template. Midiverb's forced stock switch widget crashed the owner's MKII (I218). Rytm MKII: saved sets that name retired modules open again; all twelve pads once read as held in stock's key table. Modding guidelines gain "Respect the instrument" (build for the instrument's own panel, no one-to-one copies). 2026-11-27 (changelog 2026-11-02..27, verification notes, module and machine docs): Octatrack base 0.8.2 skips two recorder writes to battery RAM that almost never change anything, keeps the fixes stock's checks make at power-up (I234), reads the recorder bank stock selects (I233), places big DSP effects under the words Sidechain claims (I235), caches UI-tick bookkeeping and adds MODWERK menu levels; POLY8 paused; FM Synth and UNGEMACH repriced on a medium pattern (I238). Digitakt II: added track machines (types 7-10) with their own DSP players, mixer hooks, linked voices (SETTINGS > VOICES) and Modwerk's own SHARC assembler; effect-slot and filter-type designs approved, no code yet. Model:Cycles: a status page and beta downloads. Rytm MKII: new Light Taps module. The changelog also documents a patch SysEx protocol for two Zoom effect pedals (another brand, not catalogued). 2026-11-28 (changelog 2026-11-24..28, verification 2026-11-26/27 for OT base 0.8.3, DT2 bounded transmit and the newer Digitakt/Digitone cores, OCTATRACK_DRIVING, OCTATRACK_API, ELEMOD_SOURCE_BUILDS, TEST_PROCEDURE, MODULE_PERFORMANCE, machine READMEs, DT2 LINK.md, new module READMEs and TESTING files): Octatrack base 0.8.3 reads the current Part from SRAM instead of CS1 inside the frame interrupt (one frame point saved), marks unreadable saved-set files DAMAGED and overwrites them on the next Keep, names knobs after the drawn track, counts USB Audio streams in the CPU limit, keys its attach watchdog on SET_CONFIGURATION (I243), clears stock's mass-storage replies at a USB reset (I241), logs usb_gone and stays off the bus for 10 s before a forced reconnect (I242). Known issue: a rare USB drop through a hub on a Mac, about 1 in 30 installs or removals. Digitakt and Digitone sets are pinned to elekloader core 4.4 and core-dn1 5.4; the builder falls back to the older core when a set does not combine (Digi EQ 1.0.2 needs core 2.1, KitBank 0.2.0 core 2.x), and CC Names now builds beside DIGISLICER. Modwerk now imports FLEXMODS' Ctrl All, Kit A/B, Real Units and Track Solo, DT-FM 1.2.1 and MIDI Loopback 1.6 for the Digitakt, and DigiHoard, DigiPrism, DigiReel, DigiSwarm, DigiTide, DigiTriad and MUTINY for the Digitone, as the authors' released .elemod files, unchanged; none has run on a unit in Modwerk. Track Solo needs the seq-events dependency, so it cannot sit beside Euclidean (same step-fire sites). Set pages warn when modules have no CPU cost measured on a unit, after large Rytm sets froze a unit on a livestream (I248). Digitakt II: an offline USB binding preflight only, no responder yet. The compiler check now refuses GCC 16.2 objects where the late-combine pass folds a post-increment load and an indexed store (stores one byte late on the ColdFire); -fno-late-combine-instructions avoids it. 2026-11-28 (later changelog, FRONTEND_MCP): the site's Status page now says when an Octatrack drops sound to keep up (50 or more frame-guard skips in a minute, read from one log page every 16 s) and names the tracks.

### Overwitch

Multitrack Overbridge audio on Linux. Supports Overbridge 2 devices incl. Analog Heat, Heat MKII and Heat +FX, Digitakt I/II, Digitone I/II/Keys, Syntakt. GPL-3.0, 671 commits. 2026-11-18 (README, docs/adding.md on main, no release yet): Overbridge 1 devices (Analog Four MKI, Analog Keys, Analog Rytm MKI) are supported with recent OS versions that speak the Overbridge 2 protocol (e.g. A4 MKI OS 1.56); only the Analog Four MKI is tested. Their track layout is set per device and can be written to the device from the GUI; their blocks hold 1 ms of audio (1-5 blocks, default 3).

_Latest seen (2026-10-31, secondary directories): altstrument: v2.2 (2025-12-21), GPL-3.0-or-later, JACK clients streaming multitrack Overbridge 2 audio._

_Related: builds on `dtdump` (README: based on the Overbridge USB reverse engineering in dtdump) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

_Sources: GitHub README, lapin-list, README, docs/adding.md (2026-11-18)_

### Sidecar | Expander

A Raspberry Pi 4B/5 on the Rytm's USB port adds digital voices, effects and a sequencer; the Rytm runs a patched OS. 0.3.2 adds experimental, emulator-only Digitakt support. The Teensy variant is frozen. GPL-2.0. On 2026-11-09, Analog Four MKII support since 0.4.0 (A4 firmware a4-v0.12, OS 1.56); 0.4.3 caps the Rytm screen redraws after users saw a sluggish Rytm at 20-40 redraws a second. 2026-11-13: a card config editor on the documentation site writes the Pi's config.txt and cmdline.txt in the browser. 2026-11-15 (INSTALL-PI): from Sidecar 0.5.0 a release is to ship a starter zip that fills one FAT32 card with the boot files, a new web app (in a hidden folder), every user machine and effect, starter content and demo samples; without the web-app folder the Pi serves the classic page. 2026-11-16 (README, RELEASE-NOTES 0.5.0, KNOWN-ISSUES, docs): 0.5.0 drops the OS 1.73 build; the Pi 5 is now the recommended board (2 GB minimum, 4 GB recommended); MORPH, the looper and sidechain moved to 0.5.1. The 0.5.0 features are marked in testing on their pages. The voices clipped at the stock Rytm's track ceiling in 0.4.x and now play 9 dB lower. Do not combine with newer elekloader cores: they store their settings in the bytes Sidecar uses. 2026-11-18 (README, RELEASE-NOTES 0.5.1, docs): 0.5.1 updates only the Pi, from the web page (a .scu file, a trial boot, automatic return to 0.5.0 if it does not come back). MORPH, the looper, sidechain and a new WAVETABLE moved again, to 0.5.2. A catalog in the web page installs community user machines from a public registry (trigcondition/sidecar-machines): native code, no sandbox, not tested by Sidecar. A USB host that vanished mid-traffic on the Pi's USB-C port halted the Pi in 0.5.0; 0.5.1 recovers. 2026-11-22 (docs: troubleshooting, web UI, start here): the docs for the coming 0.5.2 add a Lag now button that writes a marker into the Sidecar's black box log when the Rytm feels slow while the Sidecar is attached, and a procedure for sending that log (about the last 1.5 to 3 hours, in two files under /.rytm). 0.5.1 is still the current release. 2026-11-23 (README, RELEASE-NOTES 0.5.1.1, INSTALL-PI, docs install-pi, patch-and-flash, start-here, upgrading, what-works-now): Sidecar 0.5.1.1 (2026-11-22) is a fixes release. The Pi update works alone, also with the Rytm on firmware 0.5.0; the optional Rytm firmware 0.5.1.1 (OS 1.74 only) stops stock Rytm samples playing under Sidecar machines (I195) and fixes the SMPL key. A 0.5.0 or 0.5.1 Pi cannot compare a four-part version, so the first update needs "Install it anyway". New: black box download with secrets masked, catalog audio previews, a Lag now marker. MORPH, the looper, sidechain and WAVETABLE stay in 0.5.2. 2026-11-25: 0.5.1.2 (I210): /status gains hellos and capsKnown; updating from 0.5.0 or 0.5.1 still needs Install it anyway once. MORPH, the looper, sidechain, MIDI learn rows and WAVETABLE are due in 0.5.2. 2026-11-28 (README, RELEASE-NOTES 0.5.2, KNOWN-ISSUES, INSTALL-PI, PATCHER, docs): 0.5.2 needs the Pi update first, then the Rytm's two .elemod files or the patcher build for OS 1.74. WAVETABLE in old projects sounds different (WARP above 14 maps to the new warps, chords are gone, P13-P16 are new parameters). Sidechain DUCK on a Rytm track or AUDIO IN needs Overbridge mode; PUMP keys off a track's MIDI trigs. Scenes are saved per kit on the Pi's card, never in the Rytm's kit or pattern. The elekloader builder pin moved to 2bcafa1.

### Sidecar | Expander: Rytm mods

The source of the Analog Rytm MKII OS mods that Sidecar | Expander needs: patch sources, symbol map, allocation registry and the build that turns the user's own stock .syx into a modded one, as one elekloader module per OS; the Analog Four MKII's mod in a4/. 0.4.0 reports each track's pan and route (stereo through mode), adds MD's own page, preset browsers for JUNO and 6-OP FM, DSP SAMPLE's sample picker, list knobs of up to 36 names, a MIDI machine (machine 50) and arpeggiator settings in the sound. Sidecar Mini (Teensy) is frozen at 0.1.0. 2026-11-16 (v0.5.0): SAMPLER as machine 43, the Rytm's own sound parameters moved from the Pi (an offset or override added in the audio interrupt, never written to the kit), UP + RIGHT for FILL, a browser preview and file menu, send effect BASE/WIDTH. It needs elekloader core 0.1: newer cores keep their settings in the same bytes and the set is refused as an overlap. A mod SysEx report sent between the parts of a stock pattern dump cut the dump; fixed in 0.5.0 (I111). 2026-11-23 (tag v0.5.1.1: README, ELEKLOADER.md, 0021-ext and 0026-remote-ui design notes, mod.toml, re/os/1.74.toml, symbols, allocations, tools/emu README): Rytm firmware 0.5.1.1 is 0.5.0 plus two fixes. A 0.4.4 user heard stock Rytm samples under PLAITS and SOPHIE: zeroing the voice's sample gain scaled only one buffer. Now the stock sample player skips voices under a Sidecar machine and their output is zeroed before the mixer (I195). The SMPL key no longer opens the empty stock waveform page. 4,329 emulator checks, 9/9 flash rehearsals; no unit run stated. 2026-11-28 (tag v0.5.2, README, CONTRIBUTING, new AGENTS.md, ELEKLOADER, design notes 0021/0025/0026/0027/0029, re/os 1.73/1.74, registry/allocations.toml): a new allocation registry declares a 3 MB DDR pool 0x47c00000-0x47f00000 for the bundle's buffers (UI and MIDI task buffers only, zeroed on first use), the same range Modwerk's own linker uses (O51). CONTRIBUTING keeps an 8 KB reserve in elekloader's area. The guard also refuses elekloader cores 0.13 and 0.19. Stock's save keeps at most 71 lock rows and drops the rest without a warning; 0.5.2 refuses such a lock with stock's own message (SB45). The repo's agent rules forbid agents to flash or contact a device and keep firmware bytes out of the repo. The 0.5.1.1 .elemod hash is given differently in different docs (not resolved here).

_Related: same project `sidecar-expander` (README: the Rytm mods that Sidecar | Expander uses); mod for `elekloader` (README: one elekloader module per OS) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

### elkbench (hardware tests as an MCP server)

One local MCP server per PC that gives AI agent sessions the same tools for testing Elektron units (Analog Rytm MKII, Analog Four MKII, Digitone; Digitakt untested on hardware) and their emulators: claim a unit, run a test plan, flash an OS, take screenshots, record and check USB audio, take or restore an Overbridge Total Recall image. It enforces one owner per unit, emulator first, and a hardware run only after the person says go. Python stdlib; Windows and Linux. 2026-11-10: a flash between two fixed OS files of a unit can reuse an emulator pass of the same flash, recorded with the hashes of the emulator, the flash tool and the card, while all of them stay the same. 2026-11-11 (config example): an optional emulator headroom check waits for CPU, free RAM and a cap on running emulators before each emulator start. 2026-11-12: emulator timing (analog-emu unit or exact timing, the Sidecar's Overbridge stream on the Rytm) and a CPU gate that fails an emulator run at 95 % CPU. 2026-11-13: elklock marks a unit that stalled on its restart after a flash and refuses every device command on it until a watched power cycle (elkflash usb-cycle). 2026-11-14: DIN MIDI interfaces are configured per interface, not per unit; at a run's first DIN step elkbench probes each interface with the unit's working-kit dump request and uses the one that answers, so a cable can move between units without a config change; elklock locks each interface as its own device.

_Related: uses tool `analog-emu` (README: emulator first; sidecar-emu reaches analog-emu through it) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

_Sources: state/NEW.md 2026-11-10, README, README, config.example.toml (2026-11-14)_

### sidecar-emu (Sidecar emulator)

QEMU cut down to the Raspberry Pi 4B and the devices Sidecar's engine needs: boots the Sidecar engine image, answers over Ethernet, puts an Analog Rytm MKII stand-in on its USB-A side and gives its USB-C gadget a raw MIDI TCP port, so an OS upgrade or an elkbench run can go through the emulated Pi into analog-emu. A local experiment, not meant for QEMU upstream. 2026-11-19 (README): a usb-teensy device stands in for the Teensy 4.1 relay of the Sidecar firmware (its link protocol and the HalfKay bootloader, with fault options for flows that failed on the unit), behind an emulated high-speed USB hub, so a Teensy flash through the Pi can be rehearsed in the emulator. 2026-11-22 (README): an Analog Four MKII stand-in (usb-a4, USB id 1935:0b47, same link protocol as the Rytm stand-in: 256-byte blocks in for 8 channels, 200-byte blocks out for 6) makes a two-box Pi possible, with a gate script that boots, unplugs and replugs the Rytm and the A4 in both orders. The emulated Pi now has its SD card on EMMC2 as the real Pi 4. The Digitakt is not modelled. 2026-11-23 (README): several gate runs can share one host: stubs link over unix sockets in a private folder and forwarded ports fall back to free ones. 2026-11-27 (README): a Digitakt (mk1) stand-in, usb-digitakt (USB id 1935:0b2c), speaks the same link protocol with 368-byte blocks in for 12 channels (MAIN, tracks 1-8, INPUT) and 88-byte blocks out for 2, taken from the Sidecar firmware's device profile table; nothing of the Digitakt's firmware is in it and no Digitakt emulator stands behind it (a stub plays a sine on MAIN). The two-box gate now takes any pair of Rytm, A4 and Digitakt in both attach orders and can check the engine's slots and per-box voice requests (Rytm 8, A4 4, Digitakt 8).

_Related: uses tool `analog-emu` (README: through the emulated Pi into analog-emu); cites `sidecar-expander` (README: emulates the Sidecar engine) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

### telos (elekloader OS)

An elekloader build that is flashed once and then links more mods at every boot from a store on the unit, so new mods need no new firmware: .elemod files go over USB (SysEx with the non-commercial id 0x7D, each file read back and checked by CRC-32), and a MODS (TELOS) page at the end of SETTINGS switches them on or off for the next boot. A boot that crashes within 10 s of linking makes the next boot link nothing (one safe boot). Only +Drive-style mods (code and .bss, no patch sites). On the Digitone mk1 the store is 2 MB of raw +Drive sectors outside every area stock uses, so it never shows in Transfer; up to 63 files. Planned for the other devices elekloader supports. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-15; README read 2026-11-15. 2026-11-17: the Octatrack port is in the repo (octatrack/, 0.4, emulator only): .elemod files on the CF card in /ELEKLOADER/MODS (copied by USB DISK MODE or a card reader) are linked at the card's first mount, before the project load; unlike the Digitone's, these mods may patch the OS (sites), checked against stock bytes, written with interrupts masked when no task is stopped inside a site, and refused when the OS already ran them before the mount (code 23). 14 of the shop's 15 non-USB octabam conversions link together (about 61 KB); USB mods stay flash-only. DSP code from the card goes through elekloader's dspload-ot. On both devices each saved project now keeps the list of mods that ran, and loading one whose mods differ offers to switch them (LOAD PROJECT MODS?). A poc branch adds site-writing and memory-region mods for the Digitone (POC.md). 2026-11-22 (README, ar2/ and a4mk2/ README and mod.json, vendor/drive-loader-*): ports for the Analog Rytm MKII (ar2/, 0.1, OS 1.74, core-ar2 0.18) and the Analog Four MKII (a4mk2/, 0.3, OS 1.56, core-a4mk2 0.10). Both are elekloader's Drive Loaders copied unchanged into vendor/ and shipped under TELOS's name; only the SETTINGS row is TELOS's own. The module id stays drive-loader, so a build holds TELOS or the Drive Loader, never both, and +Drive mods for the Drive Loader load unchanged. Mods go to /mods through the unit's own data transfer (Elektron Transfer, Elektroid). The A4 keeps them in raw +Drive sectors that FORMAT +DRIVE empties. Projects do not yet keep their mods on either device. Neither port has run in an emulator or on a unit.

_Related: builds on `elekloader` (README: part of elekloader; built as an elekloader mod with core-dn1 and its +Drive boot linker) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

### trig-seedr

Offline pattern algorithms as an elekloader mod, opened as a third TRIG page after EUCLIDEAN: generate rhythms, notes, accents, trig conditions, retrigs and sample locks for a track, audition takes with undo, apply groove timing and velocity, and rotate a track or the whole pattern. Everything it writes is ordinary pattern data that plays and saves on a stock OS. Analog Four MKII and Syntakt are planned. Groove tables can be made from the user's own Ableton Live grooves; none are shipped. The author names Claude as coding assistant. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-15; README and firmware notes read 2026-11-15. 2026-11-16 (v0.4.0/v0.4.1, README 0.5): navigation is LEFT/RIGHT, PAGE and the TRIG keys stay stock's while the page is open. 0.4.1 is the build to flash: 0.4.0 wrote new trigs without the stock SYN/SMP/ENV flag bits, and a compiler optimisation (store merging in m68k-elf-gcc 16.2) broke a step move in the emulator (I112). Recipes live in RAM only and are lost at power-off or a pattern change. The MAP source copies Grids' drum map (GPL-3.0, Mutable Instruments, not catalogued). 2026-11-17 (v0.5.0-v0.7.0, README, release notes, flashing, testing, firmware notes): first hardware passes on a Rytm MKII (0.5.1, 0.6.0). Since 0.5.1 YES writes a take only with grid recording on and a take stays only after FUNC + YES; changing track or pattern, closing or turning RECORD off restores the original. Fuzzing found that two lock lanes on one parameter lost locks (the Rytm keeps one lock per parameter and step); refused since 0.6.0. The mod is 62 KB of code and 107 KB of RAM. Planned after 1.0: a TURING page that rewrites the track at each loop end. 2026-11-18 (v0.7.1, README, manual, flashing, testing, status M2.6): 0.7 is declared a beta for users; feedback decides what changes before 1.0. 0.7.1 fixes YOLO: take() fell off its end without a return value, so whether a roll stayed depended on a leftover register; the emulator passed by chance (I142). The mod now builds with -Werror=return-type. Boot screen shows T071 (a patch release shows Txyz, a minor one TSxy). 2026-11-20 (README, docs/firmware-notes-st142.md, flashing-st.md, plan-syntakt.md, status S0.2-U3, mods/*-st, manual): a Syntakt OS 1.42 port is in development, tested in analog-emu only (102 emulator checks), with no file offered to flash; the beta stays Rytm-only, so `devices` stays analog-rytm. The mod's code is split into a device-neutral frame/ and one part per device. On the Syntakt it uses a minimal hook-bus core of its own (456 bytes, from Synfact's GPL sources) because Synfact's core-st 2.0.3 does not link with gcc 16.2, so it does not run beside Synfact's mods. Code and data sit at 0x47a00000-0x47b00000, a range the emulator never saw the OS use; a canary mod is to check that on a unit with all 64 sample slots loaded. Differences from the Rytm: no retrigs, accent or slide; NOTE only (chord notes kept); LOCK lists the track's machine's controls; no lock-row limit. The unit file is stock 1.42 rebuilt by elektron-firmware-tool with only MAIN changed. A device header (st_params.h) is generated from the user's own stock file and never committed. Unit steps planned: practise the startup-menu recovery, flash a round-tripped stock file, the canary, then the mod. Rytm manual: YES + SCENE does not save a pattern while the mod is open (the mod takes YES, SCENE closes it). 2026-11-21 (v0.8.0, README, release-0.8, flashing-st, testing, requirements, adding-a-device, site device pages): 0.8.0 makes the Syntakt (OS 1.42) a second device, "ready for testing" (beta), so `devices` now lists it. Its first hardware pass (2026-11-19, one unit, on the 0.7.1-labelled build of the same code) went in steps: the startup-menu way back on stock, a stock file round-tripped by elektron-firmware-tool, a memory canary over 0x478b0000-0x47bf0000 with all 64 sample slots loaded (OK), then the 15 first checks, including a take kept across a power off (I184). The Rytm build of 0.8.0 is the same instrument on reorganised code and has no unit pass yet. Analog Four MKII and Digitone II are named as the next devices (docs/adding-a-device.md). 2026-11-25: v0.9.0 TURING (DJVU, CRPT and SHFT modes) works as a RHYTHM source, as a value source for NOTE, VEL and LOCK, and as a live page that rewrites steps behind the playhead; SCALE (19 scales) and ROOT on NOTE. YOLO does not roll TURING. The Syntakt build drops the Live groove tables to fit (swing grooves only). Credits name Marbles, the Labyrinth manual and the Turing Machine (descriptions only).

### LEDrum (Sidecar drum voice)

A drum voice for the Sidecar expander (a Raspberry Pi beside the Analog Rytm MKII) as a Pi user machine (.rmp): a modified port of the open-source Erica Synths LXR-02 drum voice, rewritten for float processing at 48 kHz with new envelopes and filter; the LXR wavetables and transient samples are used unchanged. Listed in the Sidecar community machine registry. Native code with no sandbox. Not affiliated with Erica Synths or Elektron. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-18.

_Related: mod for `sidecar-expander` (README: a user machine for Sidecar, installed into /Plugins on its SD card) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

### Sidecar community machine registry

The registry of community user machines and effects for the Sidecar expander (.rmp packages built for the Pi 4, Pi 5 or Teensy), from which Sidecar's web catalogue installs them. Each package comes with a manifest (id, version, board, plugin API, SHA-256, licence) and a README; tools/check.py validates a submission without loading it (header magic, format, API, board, sizes, CRC-32, relocations) and refuses changes to published files. The packages are native code with no sandbox. Most are by trigcondition, several by amnmkkr (LEDrum among them). Was a candidate (2026-11-18); read 2026-11-19. 2026-11-20 (README, CONTRIBUTING.md, docs/index-format.md): a version may carry 1-8 MP3 audio previews (at most 2 MB each, 10 MB a version) for the catalogue page; the checker validates their names and MP3 frame chain without decoding; previews are not covered by the package's SHA-256. No new packages. 2026-11-21 (machines/tapedelay2/1.1.0/README.md): TAPEDELAY2 1.1.0 (amnmkkr's port of Airwindows' TapeDelay2, Pi 5, send-effect slot) puts the resonance on the fourth knob (Smear) and fixes flutter; TIME can sync to the Rytm's tempo. Projects saved with 1.0.0 would read Flutter as Smear, so 1.1.0 is not compatible with them. Tested on a Pi 5 by the porter; no Rytm-side facts. 2026-11-22 (machines/fx.zphase/1.0.0, machines/wavesurfer/1.0.1 READMEs): new ZPHASE send effect (Airwindows' ZNotch2 swept by an LFO, free or synced, 1-4 stacked notches, MIT port by trigcondition). WAVESURFER 1.0.1 (amnmkkr's port of Bastl's Kastle 2 Wave Bard sample player, MIT) asks the Sidecar for a sample only on a trig: in 1.0.0 an LFO on its sample knobs made the Sidecar load several samples a second from the card, which went with frequent resets of a Pi 5; the README also asks for samples under 12 MB and 60 s, as longer reads went with USB drops and resets (Sidecar 0.5.1). Each voice uses about 140 KB of arena. See I186.
